title: Splitwise: Efficient Generative LLM Inference Using Phase Splitting
problem: LLM inference consists of two phases with distinct resource characteristics: a compute-intensive prompt computation phase and a memory-intensive token generation phase. Current systems fail to exploit these differences, causing compute underutilization during token generation despite state-of-the-art batching techniques.
motivation: GPU deployments for LLM inference are expensive and power-hungry, making efficiency improvements critical for scaling production services cost-effectively.
method: Splitwise splits LLM inference across two machines, each optimized for its phase's hardware needs. A high-compute GPU handles the prompt phase—reading your input and beginning the response—which is very compute-intensive. A lower-power machine handles token generation—producing output sequentially—which is memory-intensive and needs fast memory access. Machines exchange request state via fast back-plane interconnects, enabling phase-specific optimization in a heterogeneous GPU cluster.
key_novelty: The insight that LLM inference's two phases have such different hardware requirements—computing the prompt versus generating tokens—that they can be efficiently split across specialized machines.
contributions: Characterization of distinct latency, throughput, memory, and power profiles for prompt computation vs. token generation phases
Splitwise system that partitions inference requests across heterogeneous machines optimized per phase
Efficient state transfer protocols using optimized network libraries over cluster interconnects
Demonstration achieving 1.4x throughput at 20% lower cost compared to homogeneous GPU clusters

metrics.speedup: 1.4x throughput at 20% lower cost; 2.35x throughput under same power/cost budget

baselines: homogeneous GPU clusters with state-of-the-art batching and scheduling
primary_theme: Phase-aware resource specialization for LLM inference
